title: Rigveda 9.21: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.21: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.21 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 676r-676v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.21.1-3 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 676r
translation.original_text:
1e̱te dhā̍va̱ntīnda̍va̱ḥ somā̱ indrā̍ya̱ ghṛṣva̍yaḥ | ma̱tsa̱rāsa̍ḥ sva̱rvida̍ḥ ||
2pra̱vṛ̱ṇvanto̍ abhi̱yuja̱ḥ suṣva̍ye varivo̱vida̍ḥ | sva̱yaṁ sto̱tre va̍ya̱skṛta̍ḥ ||
3vṛthā̱ krīḻa̍nta̱ inda̍vaḥ sa̱dhastha̍m a̱bhy eka̱m it | sindho̍r ū̱rmā vy a̍kṣaran ||
translation.text:
1To Indra flow these running drops, these Somas frolicsome in mood. Exhilarating, finding light;
2Driving off foes, bestowing room upon the presser, willingly Bringing their praiser vitalforce.
3Lightly disporting them, the drops flow to one common reservoir, And fall into the river's wave.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 676r (numbered 98r by the scribe) (OPenn image 676, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.20.1 ‹avyaḥ vārebhiḥ arṣati sahvān›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 676v (numbered 98v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.21.4 ‹-pavamānāsaḥ āśata hitāḥ na›. Verses 9.21.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1ete | dhāvanti | indavaḥ | somāḥ | indrāya | ghṛṣvayaḥ | matsarāsaḥ | svaḥ-vidaḥ
2pra-vṛṇvantaḥ | abhi-yujaḥ | susvaye | varivaḥ-vidaḥ | svayam | stotre | vayaḥ-kṛtaḥ
3vṛthā | krīḷantaḥ | indavaḥ | sadha-stham | abhi | ekam | it | sindhoḥ | ūrmā | vi | akṣaran

translation.original_ref: RV 9.21.4-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 11); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 676v
translation.original_text:
4e̱te viśvā̍ni̱ vāryā̱ pava̍mānāsa āśata | hi̱tā na sapta̍yo̱ rathe̍ ||
5āsmi̍n pi̱śaṅga̍m indavo̱ dadhā̍tā ve̱nam ā̱diśe̍ | yo a̱smabhya̱m arā̍vā ||
6ṛ̱bhur na rathya̱ṁ nava̱ṁ dadhā̍tā̱ keta̍m ā̱diśe̍ | śu̱krāḥ pa̍vadhva̱m arṇa̍sā ||
7e̱ta u̱ tye a̍vīvaśa̱n kāṣṭhā̍ṁ vā̱jino̍ akrata | sa̱taḥ prāsā̍viṣur ma̱tim ||
translation.text:
4These Pavamânas have obtained all blessings much to be desired, Like coursers harnessed to a car.
5With view to us, O Soma-drops, bestow his manifold desire On him who yet hath given us naught.
6Bring us our wish with this design, as a wright brings his new-wrought wheel: Flow pure and shining with the stream.
7These drops have cried with resonant voice: like swift steeds they have run the course, And roused the good man's hymn to life.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 676v (numbered 98v by the scribe) (OPenn image 677, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.21.4 ‹-pavamānāsaḥ āśata hitāḥ na›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 677r (numbered 99r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.22.7 ‹gavyāni dhārayaḥ tatam tantum›. Verses 9.21.4-7 end on this page; 9.21.4 begins on fol. 676r (numbered 98r by the scribe).

5ā | asmin | piśaṅgam | indavaḥ | dadhāta | venam | ādiśe | yaḥ | asmabhyam | arāvā
6ṛbhuḥ | na | rathyam | navam | dadhāta | ketam | ādiśe | śukrāḥ | pavadhvam | arṇasā
7ete | oṃ iti | tye | avīvaśan | kāṣṭhām | vājinaḥ | akrata | sataḥ | pra | asāviṣuḥ | matim
